claim: A large-scale RNA interference (RNAi) screen was performed to identify genes whose loss of expression confer anoikis resistance.
source: To investigate the possibility that there are additional factors and regulatory pathways that promote anoikis, we performed a large-scale RNA interference (RNAi) screen for genes whose loss of expression confer anoikis resistance.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental design and execution of the RNAi screen.

claim: The RNAi screen was performed in MCF10A cells, an immortalized but non-transformed human breast epithelial cell line.
source: The screen was performed in MCF10A cells, an immortalized but non-transformed human breast epithelial cell line that has been frequently used to study anoikis (see, for example, Huang et al., 2010; Reginato et al., 2003; Schmelzle et al., 2007; Taube et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript states the cell line used and cites previous studies using this cell line for anoikis research.

claim: A genome-wide human small hairpin RNA (shRNA) library comprising ~62,400 shRNAs directed against ~28,000 genes was used for the screen.
source: A genome-wide human small hairpin RNA (shRNA) library comprising ~62,400 shRNAs directed against ~28,000 genes (Silva et al., 2003; Silva et al., 2005) was divided into 10 pools, which were packaged into retroviral particles and used to stably transduce MCF10A cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the library used and cites the sources for the library.

claim: Bioinformatic analysis identified 26 shRNAs whose abundance was significantly enriched >500-fold following detachment.
source: Bioinformatic analysis of the two populations identified 26 shRNAs whose abundance was significantly enriched >500-fold following detachment (Figure 1—source data 1); such shRNAs presumably confer upon MCF10A cells a selective advantage by protecting them from undergoing anoikis.
evidence: The manuscript reports the results of bioinformatic analysis of sequencing data.

claim: Knockdown of BIM decreased cell death following detachment compared to the control non-silencing (NS) shRNA.
source: As expected, knockdown of BIM, a positive control, decreased cell death following detachment compared to the control non-silencing (NS) shRNA (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes the result of BIM knockdown and references Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 showing the data.

claim: Five candidate shRNAs reduced the level of detachment-induced apoptosis compared to the NS shRNA.
source: Of the 20 candidate shRNAs tested, five reduced the level of detachment-induced apoptosis compared to the NS shRNA, indicating they conferred anoikis resistance (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports the validation results and references Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: KDM3A was one of the top scoring validated candidates from the RNAi screen.
source: One of the top scoring validated candidates was KDM3A (Figure 1—source data 1), a histone demethylase that specifically demethylates mono-methylated (me1) and di-methylated (me2) histone H3 lysine 9 (H3K9) (Yamane et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript identifies KDM3A as a top candidate and cites the reference for its demethylase activity.

claim: KDM3A is a histone demethylase that specifically demethylates mono-methylated (me1) and di-methylated (me2) histone H3 lysine 9 (H3K9).
source: One of the top scoring validated candidates was KDM3A (Figure 1—source data 1), a histone demethylase that specifically demethylates mono-methylated (me1) and di-methylated (me2) histone H3 lysine 9 (H3K9) (Yamane et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript describes the enzymatic activity of KDM3A and cites the reference.

claim: H3K9 methylation is a transcriptional repressive mark.
source: H3K9 methylation is a transcriptional repressive mark, and the identification of KDM3A raised the intriguing possibility that induction of anoikis involves transcriptional activation of specific genes through H3K9me1/2 demethylation.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge.

claim: Ectopic expression of wild-type KDM3A but not KDM3A(H1120G/D1122N) greatly reduced MCF10A cell viability.
source: The results of Figure 1C show that ectopic expression of wild-type KDM3A but not KDM3A(H1120G/D1122N) greatly reduced MCF10A cell viability.
evidence: The manuscript reports the results shown in Figure 1C.

claim: KDM3A is necessary and sufficient for efficient induction of anoikis in breast epithelial cells.
source: Collectively, the results of Figure 1 demonstrate that KDM3A is necessary and sufficient for efficient induction of anoikis in breast epithelial cells.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the findings from Figure 1 experiments.

claim: KDM3A protein levels were very low in attached MCF10A cells, but robustly increased in a time-dependent manner following detachment.
source: The immunoblot of Figure 2A shows that KDM3A protein levels were very low in attached MCF10A cells, but robustly increased in a time-dependent manner following detachment.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: An increase in KDM3A expression following detachment was also detected at the mRNA level.
source: The qRT-PCR analysis of Figure 2B shows that an increase in KDM3A expression following detachment was also detected at the mRNA level.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Anoikis is suppressed by integrin signaling, which functions through FAK, a regulator of the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway.
source: As mentioned above, anoikis is suppressed by integrin signaling, which functions through FAK, a regulator of the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway (Frisch et al., 1996; King et al., 1997).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies establishing this signaling pathway.

claim: Detachment causes a disruption in integrin–ECM contacts, resulting in a loss of FAK signaling in the detached cells.
source: Detachment causes a disruption in integrin–ECM contacts, resulting in a loss of FAK signaling in the detached cells (Frisch and Francis, 1994; Frisch et al., 1996), which we observed have elevated KDM3A levels (see Figures 2A and B).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies and references their own data.

claim: The addition of Matrigel basement membrane-like matrix to detached cells markedly blocked the elevated levels of BIMEL and KDM3A.
source: The results of Figure 2C show that the addition of Matrigel basement membrane-like matrix, which restores integrin signaling, to detached cells markedly blocked the elevated levels of the BIM isoform BIMEL, as expected, and KDM3A.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Treatment of MCF10A cells with a FAK inhibitor increased the levels of KDM3A protein and mRNA.
source: Treatment of MCF10A cells with a FAK inhibitor increased the levels of KDM3A protein (Figure 2D) and mRNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The increase in KDM3A levels upon detachment of MCF10A cells is due, at least in part, to the loss of integrin/FAK signaling.
source: Thus, the increase in KDM3A levels upon detachment of MCF10A cells is due, at least in part, to the loss of integrin/FAK signaling.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the findings from the FAK experiments.

claim: Expression of either EGFR or MEK2DD substantially decreased the level of BIMEL in detached MCF10A cells.
source: Consistent with these previous results, Figure 2E shows that in detached MCF10A cells, expression of either EGFR or MEK2DD substantially decreased the level of BIMEL (Reginato et al., 2003).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 2E and cites a previous study.

claim: Expression of either EGFR or MEK2DD decreased the levels of KDM3A in detached MCF10A cells.
source: Expression of either EGFR or MEK2DD also decreased the levels of KDM3A in detached MCF10A cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 2E.

claim: KDM3A protein levels were increased in attached MCF10A cells treated with the EGFR inhibitor gefitinib or the MEK inhibitor U0126.
source: Conversely, KDM3A protein levels were increased in attached MCF10A cells treated with the EGFR inhibitor gefitinib (Barker et al., 2001; Ward et al., 1994) (Figure 2F) or the MEK inhibitor U0126 (Favata et al., 1998) (Figure 2G).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 2F and 2G and cites references for the inhibitors.

claim: Both gefitinib and U0126 treatment resulted in increased KDM3A mRNA levels.
source: Both gefitinib and U0126 treatment also resulted in increased KDM3A mRNA levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Following detachment, expression of BNIP3 and BNIP3L increased, and were the only genes whose expression was diminished more than 2-fold by KDM3A knockdown.
source: By contrast, following detachment, expression of BNIP3 and BNIP3L increased, and were the only genes whose expression was diminished more than 2-fold by KDM3A knockdown (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of BIM and BMF increased upon detachment.
source: Consistent with previous results (Reginato et al., 2003; Schmelzle et al., 2007), expression of BIM and BMF were increased upon detachment.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding and cites previous studies.

claim: Knockdown of KDM3A did not decrease expression of either BIM or BMF.
source: However, knockdown of KDM3A did not decrease expression of either BIM or BMF.
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding from the qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: BNIP3 and BNIP3L protein levels were very low in attached cells and substantially increased following detachment.
source: The immunoblot of Figure 3B shows that BNIP3 and BNIP3L levels were very low in attached cells and substantially increased following detachment, with a time course similar to that of detachment-induced KDM3A expression (see Figure 2A).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: KDM3A was bound to the BNIP3 and BNIP3L promoters in detached but not attached cells.
source: The chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) experiment of Figure 3C shows that KDM3A was bound to the BNIP3 and BNIP3L promoters in detached but not attached cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The levels of H3K9me2 on the BNIP3 and BNIP3L promoters were greatly diminished following detachment, which was counteracted by knockdown of KDM3A.
source: Moreover, the levels of H3K9me2 (Figure 3D) and H3K9me1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) on the BNIP3 and BNIP3L promoters were greatly diminished following detachment, which was counteracted by knockdown of KDM3A.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Overexpression of KDM3A but not KDM3A(H1120G/D1122N) in attached MCF10A cells resulted in decreased levels of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2 on the BNIP3 and BNIP3L promoters and increased expression of BNIP3 and BNIP3L.
source: Conversely, overexpression of KDM3A but not KDM3A(H1120G/D1122N) in attached MCF10A cells resulted in decreased levels of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2 on the BNIP3 and BNIP3L promoters and increased expression of BNIP3 and BNIP3L (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Knockdown of BNIP3 or BNIP3L resulted in decreased apoptosis following detachment.
source: Finally, knockdown of BNIP3 or BNIP3L (Figure 3—figure supplement 4) resulted in decreased apoptosis following detachment (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Moderate cell death was observed upon ectopic expression of either BNIP3 or BNIP3L, but substantial cell death occurred in cells ectopically expressing both BNIP3 and BNIP3L.
source: Figure 3F shows that moderate cell death was observed upon ectopic expression of either BNIP3 or BNIP3L, but substantial cell death occurred in cells ectopically expressing both BNIP3 and BNIP3L.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 3F.

claim: BNIP3 and BNIP3L are critical KDM3A target genes that mediate anoikis.
source: Collectively, these results establish BNIP3 and BNIP3L as critical KDM3A target genes that mediate anoikis (Figure 3G).
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the findings from the BNIP3 and BNIP3L experiments.

claim: Detachment-induced apoptosis was significantly diminished in breast cancer cell lines compared to MCF10A cells, indicative of anoikis resistance.
source: As expected, detachment-induced apoptosis was significantly diminished in breast cancer cell lines compared to MCF10A cells, indicative of anoikis resistance (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Following detachment of the breast cancer cell lines, induction of KDM3A at both the protein and mRNA levels was much lower than that observed in MCF10A cells.
source: Moreover, following detachment of the breast cancer cell lines, induction of KDM3A at both the protein (Figure 4B) and mRNA (Figure 4C) levels was much lower than that observed in MCF10A cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: Ectopic expression of KDM3A was sufficient to induce apoptosis in each of the five breast cancer cell lines.
source: However, ectopic expression of KDM3A was sufficient to induce apoptosis in each of the five breast cancer cell lines (Figure 4D).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Anoikis-resistance of human breast cancer cells is due, at least in part, to inefficient induction of KDM3A following detachment.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that anoikis-resistance of human breast cancer cells is due, at least in part, to inefficient induction of KDM3A following detachment.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the findings from the breast cancer cell line experiments.

claim: Interrogation of the Oncomine database revealed decreased expression levels of KDM3A in several breast cancer datasets.
source: Interrogation of the Oncomine database (Rhodes et al., 2007) revealed decreased expression levels of KDM3A in several breast cancer datasets (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results from the Oncomine database query and cites the database reference.

claim: Compared to normal breast epithelium KDM3A expression was significantly decreased in a high percentage of breast cancers.
source: The results of Figure 4E show that compared to normal breast epithelium KDM3A expression was significantly decreased in a high percentage of breast cancers.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Basal KDM3A expression levels were also diminished in most human breast cancer cell lines analyzed.
source: Likewise, basal KDM3A expression levels were also diminished in most human breast cancer cell lines analyzed (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Kdm3a knockdown significantly increased the number of CLS1 cells that survived in the mouse lung relative to the control NS shRNA.
source: The results of Figure 4F show that Kdm3a knockdown significantly increased the number of cells that survived in the mouse lung relative to the control NS shRNA.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4F.

claim: qRT-PCR analysis revealed decreased Kdm3a expression in cell lines with greater metastatic potential.
source: qRT-PCR analysis revealed decreased Kdm3a expression in cell lines with greater metastatic potential (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Control 67NR cells failed to form pulmonary metastases in any of the three mice analyzed.
source: The results of Figure 4G show, as expected, that control 67NR cells failed to form pulmonary metastases in any of the three mice analyzed.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Kdm3a knockdown 67NR cells formed substantial pulmonary metastases in all three mice.
source: By contrast, Kdm3a knockdown 67NR cells formed substantial pulmonary metastases in all three mice.
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The growth of primary tumors formed by NS or Kdm3a knockdown 4T07 cells was similar.
source: The growth of primary tumors formed by NS or Kdm3a knockdown cells was similar (Figure 4H and Figure 4—figure supplement 8).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4H and Figure 4—figure supplement 8.

claim: Kdm3a knockdown 4T07 cells caused significantly increased metastatic burden in the lungs compared to control 4T07 cells.
source: However, Kdm3a knockdown cells caused significantly increased metastatic burden in the lungs compared to control 4T07 cells (Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 9).
evidence: The manuscript describes the results shown in Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 9.

claim: KDM3A functions to prevent metastasis.
source: Collectively, these results show that KDM3A functions to prevent metastasis.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the findings from the in vivo metastasis experiments.

claim: Following detachment of non-transformed cells, integrin signaling is decreased leading to transcriptional induction of KDM3A.
source: Following detachment of non-transformed cells, integrin signaling is decreased leading to transcriptional induction of KDM3A.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as part of the proposed model.

claim: The increased levels of KDM3A results in its recruitment to the pro-apoptotic genes BNIP3 and BNIP3L, where it promotes demethylation of inhibitory H3K9me1/2 marks and transcriptional activation of the two genes, resulting in anoikis induction.
source: The increased levels of KDM3A results in its recruitment to the pro-apoptotic genes BNIP3 and BNIP3L, where it promotes demethylation of inhibitory H3K9me1/2 marks and transcriptional activation of the two genes, resulting in anoikis induction.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as part of the proposed model.

claim: Previous studies have shown that hypoxia results in transcriptional activation of KDM3A, BNIP3 and BNIP3L.
source: Consistent with this model, previous studies have shown that hypoxia results in transcriptional activation of KDM3A, BNIP3 and BNIP3L (Beyer et al., 2008; Sowter et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies showing this relationship.

claim: In anoikis-resistant human breast cancer cell lines and tumors, KDM3A expression is defective.
source: We have found that in anoikis-resistant human breast cancer cell lines and tumors, KDM3A expression is defective, highlighting the importance of this pathway in promoting anoikis.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the findings from the breast cancer cell line and tumor analyses.

claim: The results reveal a novel transcriptional regulatory program that mediates anoikis in non-transformed cells and is disabled during cancer development.
source: Collectively, our results reveal a novel transcriptional regulatory program that mediates anoikis in non-transformed cells and is disabled during cancer development.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as the overall conclusion.

claim: Unlike BNIP3 and BNIP3L, BIM and BMF are not regulated by KDM3A.
source: However, we have found that unlike BNIP3 and BNIP3L, BIM and BMF are not regulated by KDM3A.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding from the qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: Anoikis is promoted by multiple non-redundant pathways.
source: Thus, our results reveal that anoikis is promoted by multiple non-redundant pathways, which may help prevent the development of anoikis resistance.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the finding that BIM/BMF and BNIP3/BNIP3L are regulated by different mechanisms.

claim: Epithelial cells that lose attachment to the extracellular matrix (ECM), or attach to an inappropriate ECM, undergo a specialized form of apoptosis called anoikis.
source: Epithelial cells that lose attachment to the extracellular matrix (ECM), or attach to an inappropriate ECM, undergo a specialized form of apoptosis called anoikis.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Anoikis has an important role in preventing oncogenesis, particularly metastasis, by eliminating cells that lack proper ECM cues.
source: Anoikis has an important role in preventing oncogenesis, particularly metastasis, by eliminating cells that lack proper ECM cues (Simpson et al., 2008; Zhu et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies establishing this role of anoikis.

claim: Anoikis functions to prevent the invasion of tumor cells into the luminal space, which is a hallmark of epithelial tumors.
source: Anoikis also functions to prevent the invasion of tumor cells into the luminal space, which is a hallmark of epithelial tumors (Debnath et al., 2002).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study establishing this function of anoikis.

claim: Epithelial-derived cancers, such as breast cancer, develop resistance to anoikis.
source: In general, epithelial-derived cancers, such as breast cancer, develop resistance to anoikis (reviewed in Schwartz, 1997).
evidence: The manuscript cites a review establishing this general principle.

claim: Anoikis is suppressed by integrin signaling, which functions through focal adhesion kinase (FAK), an activator of the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway.
source: In particular, anoikis is suppressed by integrin signaling, which functions through focal adhesion kinase (FAK), an activator of the RAF/MEK/ERK pathway (King et al., 1997).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study establishing this signaling pathway.

claim: FAK signaling is active in attached cells and is inactive following detachment.
source: FAK signaling is active in attached cells and is inactive following detachment (Frisch et al., 1996).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study establishing this relationship.

claim: Anoikis is also suppressed by integrin-mediated, ligand independent activation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling pathway.
source: Anoikis is also suppressed by integrin-mediated, ligand independent activation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling pathway (Moro et al., 1998), which, like FAK, also stimulates RAF/MEK/ERK activity.
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study establishing this signaling pathway.

claim: Cell signaling pathways have been found to regulate the levels of BIM (also called BCL2L11) and BMF, two pro-apoptotic members of the BCL2 family of apoptosis regulators previously shown to contribute to anoikis.
source: These cell signaling pathways have been found to regulate the levels of BIM (also called BCL2L11) and BMF, two pro-apoptotic members of the BCL2 family of apoptosis regulators previously shown to contribute to anoikis (Reginato et al., 2003; Schmelzle et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies establishing the role of BIM and BMF in anoikis.

claim: Depletion of BIM or BMF diminishes but does not completely prevent anoikis.
source: However, depletion of BIM or BMF diminishes but does not completely prevent anoikis (Reginato et al., 2003; Schmelzle et al., 2007), suggesting the existence of other factors and regulatory pathways that can promote anoikis.
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies and infers the existence of other factors.

claim: The basis of anoikis resistance remains to be determined and to date has not been linked to alterations in expression or activity of BIM or BMF.
source: Moreover, the basis of anoikis resistance remains to be determined and to date has not been linked to alterations in expression or activity of BIM or BMF.
evidence: The manuscript states this as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Knockdown of Bnip3 has been shown to cause increased metastasis in similar in vivo experiments.
source: Consistent with our results, knockdown of Bnip3 has also been shown to cause increased metastasis in similar in vivo experiments (Manka et al., 2005).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study showing this result.

claim: In attached breast epithelial cells, KDM3A expression is maintained at low levels by integrin signaling.
source: In attached breast epithelial cells, KDM3A expression is maintained at low levels by integrin signaling.
evidence: The manuscript states this in the abstract as a summary of findings.

claim: Following detachment, integrin signaling is decreased resulting in increased KDM3A expression.
source: Following detachment, integrin signaling is decreased resulting in increased KDM3A expression.
evidence: The manuscript states this in the abstract as a summary of findings.

claim: RNAi-mediated knockdown of KDM3A substantially reduces apoptosis following detachment.
source: RNAi-mediated knockdown of KDM3A substantially reduces apoptosis following detachment and, conversely, ectopic expression of KDM3A induces cell death in attached cells.
evidence: The manuscript states this in the abstract as a summary of findings.

claim: Ectopic expression of KDM3A induces cell death in attached cells.
source: RNAi-mediated knockdown of KDM3A substantially reduces apoptosis following detachment and, conversely, ectopic expression of KDM3A induces cell death in attached cells.
evidence: The manuscript states this in the abstract as a summary of findings.

claim: KDM3A promotes anoikis through transcriptional activation of BNIP3 and BNIP3L, which encode pro-apoptotic proteins.
source: We find that KDM3A promotes anoikis through transcriptional activation of BNIP3 and BNIP3L, which encode pro-apoptotic proteins.
evidence: The manuscript states this in the abstract as a summary of findings.

claim: Knockdown of Kdm3a enhances metastatic potential in mouse models of breast cancer metastasis.
source: Using mouse models of breast cancer metastasis we show that knockdown of Kdm3a enhances metastatic potential.
evidence: The manuscript states this in the abstract as a summary of findings.

claim: There is defective KDM3A expression in human breast cancer cell lines and tumors.
source: Finally, we find defective KDM3A expression in human breast cancer cell lines and tumors.
evidence: The manuscript states this in the abstract as a summary of findings.
